[message_id=684508 author=m4nocha first=True]
I saw that people are achieving 69% accuracy with only prompt -> boxed answer mapping
on the other hand i am able to achieve only 65% accuracy with synthetic CoT SFT (for 4 easy categories only)?
do you think there is something wrong with my training pipeline? or do I need to move forward with RL?
I analysed the answer prompt on the validation set and the output reasoning trace is quite different from the training input

[message_id=3430305 author=tamura_aicon first=False]
In my experiments, I've confirmed that SFT with an improved dataset can reach a score of 0.76.

[message_id=3430315 author=Bianco Chiu first=False]
Hi, may I ask what do you mean by improved dataset, with CoT?

[message_id=3430334 author=tamura_aicon first=False]
Yes, with CoT. In my experience, data quality matters far more than quantity. Not every category benefits from the same training approach.

[message_id=3428589 author=SwiftyOS first=False]
This is something I'm wondering too. Where does RL play a part if its possible to programatically solve all the problems.

[message_id=3429812 author=m4nocha first=False]
how much did you achieve with SFT then?
